specification.objective: Replace free-form session emoji choices with user-created colored emoji tags that can be assigned to sessions.

requirements.statement: Users can create a session tag with a non-empty name, one valid emoji, and a valid six-digit hex color.
Users can assign one existing tag to a session; its emoji is shown on the session-row badge and its color is used for the badge and the SDK session color indicator.
Tag definitions and durable-session assignments persist in plugin storage and are restored after plugin reload.
Existing emoji-only session assignments remain visible until replaced or cleared, without guessing a color for them.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A user can create a named tag with an emoji and color, then assign it to a session from the plugin UI.
The session row shows the tag emoji on a badge with the tag color, and the SDK receives the same per-session color keyed by the durable session ID.
Tag definitions and assignments survive reload; clearing an applied tag clears its color override.
Legacy emoji assignments remain visible until the user replaces or clears them; no background color is guessed for legacy entries.

invariants.statement: Profile accent colors and the accent-derived app background continue to work unchanged.
The feature uses the public host.sessions.setColor API and does not modify Hermes Desktop core.
Session assignments remain keyed by durable stored session IDs.

forbidden_states.statement: A tag with an invalid name, emoji, or color is stored.
An invalid or missing tag ID is applied to a session.
Legacy emoji-only annotations are silently discarded or assigned an invented color.
The full session-row background is changed through unsupported DOM or CSS manipulation.

inputs.statement: User-entered tag name, emoji, and color; the durable ID of the target session; and existing plugin preferences.

outputs.statement: Persisted tag definitions and session-tag assignments; a colored emoji badge; and the SDK per-session color override.

failure_semantics.statement: Invalid tag input is rejected without modifying persisted preferences or session colors.
Clearing a tag removes its assignment and clears the session color override.

baseline_output_contains: Prisma supports creating and applying named session tags
